messages:
fiona: Heads-up: hit a nasty edge with streaming through our new edge-proxy. Multibyte UTF-8 characters (emoji) are getting split across TCP frames and our SDKs sometimes emit � or raise decode errors. Also the proxy injects periodic ":keepalive" comment lines which sometimes land inside a multibyte sequence.

mauro: ouch. which sdk/runtime? can you paste a tiny raw capture?

fiona: Node & Python. raw bytes (simplified hex view):

```
64 61 74 61 3a 20 7b 22 74 6f 6b 65 6e 22 3a 22 5f f0 9f 98

# <-- socket chunk boundary

9a 22 7d 0a 0a
:keepalive

64 61 74 61 3a 20 5b 44 4f 4e 45 5d 0a 0a
```

The 3-byte emoji sequence is split between packets (f0 9f 98 | 9a). When the comment line arrives between them some decoders produce U+FFFD and parsed tokens break.

asha: that's tricky. We should treat the stream as bytes until we have full UTF-8 codepoints for each event payload. Right now node-sdk uses text streaming and the runtime's TextDecoder which can handle stream mode, but our code calls decode() per recv chunk. If decode() receives an incomplete sequence it replaces by the replacement char unless streaming mode is used.

mauro: python's decode('utf-8') on bytes will raise if errors='strict', but many libs use errors='replace' for robustness which yields �. We want stable semantics: never emit replacement chars for incomplete codepoints; instead defer decoding until the event boundary is complete (or until we've got enough bytes). Also need to ensure comment lines starting with ':' are parsed at the byte level and don't split multibyte sequences.

fiona: Proposed approach: 1) switch to byte-buffered SSE parser: accumulate bytes and only attempt UTF-8 decode for a complete line (i.e., when we detect '\n' or '\r\n'). 2) use incremental decoders (TextDecoder in streaming mode or codecs.incrementaldecoder in python) so partial codepoints are buffered by decoder instead of replaced. 3) ensure comment detection is done after a successful decode of the full line.

asha: + add tests that simulate: recv() -> [b"data: {\"text\": \"Hello ", b"\xf0\x9f", b"\x98\x9a\"}\n\n"] and also the variant where a ":keepalive\n\n" lands between the split bytes. Assert final text contains the emoji only once and no replacement chars.

mauro: Also watch out for HTTP/2 DATA frame coalescing at the proxy. Some proxies will re-chunk differently in real networks; tests should randomize chunk boundaries.

tooling-bot: Issue #7120 created by fiona - title: streaming: handle split UTF-8 sequences + inline keepalive comments injected by proxy; add tests and incremental decoding.

fiona: I opened PR #4312 with a small refactor: byte-buffered base parser + incremental decoder use for node/python. Included randomized chunking tests and a quick manual sample for the edge-proxy config. Local runs + CI pass.

asha: Nice. A couple of safety nits: 1) limit incremental decoder buffer size to avoid unbounded memory if we never see newline, 2) log a debug event when we see lots of partial bytes without newline (helpful for ops).

mauro: Agreed. Also update SDK quickstart to mention that the streaming path is byte-safe and recommend using SDK helpers rather than naive text streaming for polyfilled runtimes.

tooling-bot: PR #4312 merged to main by mauro - changelog: fix(sdk): byte-buffer SSE parser and use incremental UTF-8 decoding to avoid replacement characters when multibyte codepoints are split; add randomized chunk tests and docs.

fiona: Verified in staging with edge-proxy + 1k randomized chunk trials. No replacement chars and no extra empty tokens. thanks :tada:
